title: Longitudinal Olink affinity proteomics profiling of cytokine release syndrome in myeloma patients receiving BCMA-directed CAR-T therapy
projectDescription: This submission contains de-identified Olink NPX affinity proteomics data from longitudinal peripheral blood samples collected from patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treated with BCMA-directed CAR-T therapy (ide-cel or cilta-cel) in a prospective single-center pilot study. Samples were analyzed using the Olink Target 92 Immuno-Oncology panel to characterize inflammatory protein dynamics associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS). In the associated study, these proteomic data were integrated with wearable physiologic monitoring to evaluate early CRS detection and to identify candidate biomarkers, including IFN-γ.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Peripheral blood was collected longitudinally from patients undergoing BCMA-directed CAR-T therapy into 10 mL green-top heparinized tubes during standard-of-care blood draws. Plasma was separated by centrifugation, aliquoted, and cryopreserved until analysis. De-identified plasma samples were profiled using the Olink Target 92 Immuno-Oncology panel, and protein abundances were reported as normalized protein expression (NPX) values generated with Olink NPX Signature software.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein measurements were generated using the Olink Target 96 Immuno-Oncology panel (v.3113) and processed with Olink NPX Signature v1.11.0. Quantification was based on vendor-generated NPX values, which represent normalized relative protein abundance on the log2 scale; the exported dataset includes Olink assay identifiers, UniProt identifiers, plate identifiers, and vendor QC metrics. No peptide-spectrum matching or database search was performed, as this dataset was generated using an affinity proteomics assay rather than LC-MS/MS. Downstream analyses were performed on the vendor-provided NPX matrix after review of QC annotations, using de-identified sample metadata and longitudinal sampling information. Downstream analyses included longitudinal statistical modeling of cytokine trajectories and exploratory integration with wearable-device data for cytokine release syndrome detection and prediction.
